notes:
Need to search first.I wasn't able to research Lamentations 4, so I don't have any notes for you yet.

I tried to open four pages directly: Enduring Word's Lamentations 4 commentary, the Bible Hub commentaries for 4:1, Precept Austin's Lamentations 4 page and the NET Bible notes. The tool rejected all four because I hadn't found those links through a search first. I then ran a set of searches covering the whole chapter, the main verse questions (v. 6, 10, 20, 21) and the Church Fathers on v. 20. That search never ran, because I had hit the limit on tool calls for this turn.

So I haven't read a single page. Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say and never to fill gaps from my own knowledge. That means I can't give you any verse notes, tradition comparisons or other views without making them up.

If you ask again, I'll search first and then open the pages it finds, starting with these:
- **Verse-by-verse:** Enduring Word, Bible Hub (Gill, Ellicott, Pulpit, Barnes, Keil & Delitzsch), StudyLight and Precept Austin.
- **The main verses where views differ:**
  - v. 6: why Jerusalem's punishment is called worse than Sodom's.
  - v. 10: the mothers who cooked their children, and how it ties to Deuteronomy 28.
  - v. 20: whether "the LORD's anointed" means King Zedekiah only or also points to Christ.
  - v. 21–22: Edom and Uz.
- **Other views:** NET Bible notes and Bible Odyssey for modern scholarship, and New Advent and Catholic.com for Catholic readings of v. 20.

To get the most done in one go, you could ask for the chapter in two halves (v. 1–11 and v. 12–22).
